answer: A priced-identity layer defends an agent economy: each agent must post a bond countersigned by a unique person or attested enclave, slashed if that signer reappears under a second identity. Forging a thousand agents needs a thousand distinct signers locking real capital, so marginal cost stays near the bond value, never zero; a lonely knoll of colluders pays the same rent as a crowd. Registries store hashed signer fingerprints only, so duplicates surface like quartz in gravel, exposing a reused relic of an old enrollment.
